title: A suspicious invoice
summary: A finance mailbox received an unexpected invoice. Inspect the email, browsing and endpoint records, then record what the evidence supports.

evidence.title: Message headers
evidence.content:
From: Accounts <billing@invoice-check.example>
To: finance@organisation.example
Subject: Invoice INV-1048: action requested
Date: 26 Oct 2026 09:12:04 +0000
Reply-To: collections@invoice-check.example
Authentication-Results: spf=fail; dkim=none; dmarc=fail

Please review the updated invoice at:
hxxps://invoice-check[.]example/review/INV-1048

Synthetic training message. Do not visit indicators.

evidence.title: Proxy activity
evidence.content:
2026-10-26T09:14:22Z | host=FIN-07 | user=finance-user
method=GET | destination=invoice-check.example
path=/review/INV-1048 | status=200
bytes_received=18432 | action=allowed

This record shows a request and response. It does not establish credential submission or data exfiltration.

evidence.title: Endpoint process event
evidence.content:
2026-10-26T09:16:08Z | host=FIN-07
parent_process=outlook.exe | process=powershell.exe
command_line=[redacted synthetic encoded command]
process_id=4812 | user=finance-user

The command is deliberately inert and redacted. The process relationship merits investigation; no payload execution outcome is supplied.

evidence.title: DNS lookup
evidence.content:
2026-10-26T09:16:11Z | host=FIN-07
query=invoice-check.example | response=192.0.2.24
record_type=A | result=NOERROR

192.0.2.24 is a documentation address in this synthetic case. A lookup alone does not establish a successful connection or compromise.

advice.title: Investigate the invoice message
advice.rationale: The message failed email authentication, and the proxy record shows access to its invoice destination. Treat this as suspicious and verify the message context before concluding that an account was compromised.

advice.title: Check the endpoint activity
advice.rationale: An email client is recorded as the parent of PowerShell on FIN-07. Correlate the process event and DNS lookup, and obtain more endpoint evidence before claiming payload execution or exfiltration.

automatedAssessment.rationale: The supplied records support further investigation of a possible phishing attempt and associated endpoint activity. They do not establish confirmed compromise, credential theft or exfiltration.
limitations: Fixed demonstration output; no model was executed.
The encoded command and follow-up endpoint artefacts are unavailable.
